children: Lululemon Athletica, best known for its yoga clothes and other specialty athleticwear, reported quarterly revenue that fell short of expectations.
For its second fiscal quarter ended in July, Lululemon reported sales of $2.4 billion, below the $2.458 billion Wall Street expected, and down from $2.525 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Adjusted earnings of $2.92 a share beat projections for $1.79 a share, but that included 86 cents a share from tariff refunds.
Same-store sales fell 9% during the quarter, nearly double the decline of 4.6% that analysts had projected.
Shares dropped 14%, to $104.54, in late Thursday trading, after closing up 1.4% at $121.77 in regular trading.
The stock is down 41.4% this year through Thursday's close and down 40.9% over the past 12 months, before its latest financial results were reported.
Lululemon announced in April that Heidi O'Neill would become its next CEO and join the board of directors starting Tuesday, Sept. 8.
